tasks.title: Audit closest compressed-training and dictionary-learning papers
tasks.description: Read projectIdea.md and the existing bibliography. Inspect primary sources for compressed training-data storage and dictionary capacity under compression. Prioritize Nayak/Friedland, the storage-aware learning article, Berkeley training-compression report, and the unresolved Wei et al. work. Deliver a bounded first-pass evidence matrix and structured source list; record actual access limits, measurement definitions, version differences, exact overlap, and remaining uncertainty. Do not edit the shared bibliography or promise novelty.
acceptance: Report and source evidence list exist
Each key claim has an inspected primary-source location or explicit access limitation
Actual stored bytes are distinguished from quality-factor proxies and payload-only rates
Closest overlap and unresolved novelty are stated without overclaiming

tasks.title: Design the minimum controlled training-storage experiment
tasks.description: Translate the user's latest goal into a month-sized study of learning from heavily JPEG-compressed training images. Explain a genuine neural dictionary component, fair baselines, M versus k, full-file byte accounting, split/pretraining/clean-target controls, a bounded pilot, and compute/run-count implications. Keep dataset, GPU, and accuracy target feasibility unresolved until supported. No training or downloads.
acceptance: A falsifiable research question and minimal comparison are specified
Compressed training inputs and a common held-out evaluation are explicit
Dictionary model and sparsity controls are technically meaningful
Proposed choices, known requirements, and resource unknowns are separated

tasks.title: Audit reusable model implementations and pilot requirements
tasks.description: Inspect a small number of existing neural sparse-coding or dictionary-learning implementations and conventional backbones as possible starting points. Verify accessible source code, license, environment requirements, genuine dictionary mechanism, and likely adaptation effort. Propose at most two dataset/resolution options with full-file JPEG feasibility considerations. Identify hardware information needed. This is a read-only feasibility audit; do not install dependencies, download datasets, or run training. Preserve the proposal and bibliography.
acceptance: Implementation claims link to inspected upstream sources
Unexecuted checks are labeled unexecuted
A bounded pilot and its resource needs are described
Recommendation fits the current training-storage question and month constraint

tasks.title: Independently challenge evidence and experimental reasoning
tasks.description: Read accepted LIT-001 and REASON-001 artifacts. Check a small set of consequential source claims and challenge the proposed experiment for confounding, storage accounting, hidden clean information, pretraining, scope, and unjustified novelty. Produce concrete corrections and a recommendation. This review can identify unresolved research even when source-audit tasks are complete.
acceptance: Findings cite specific source/report locations
Blocking design flaws are distinguished from optional improvements
The reviewer does not present their own prior authored report as independently reviewed
A clear next-step recommendation is recorded

tasks.title: Integrate a concrete month-sized project recommendation
tasks.description: Combine reviewed literature, reasoning, reproducibility, and critique into a proposed project plan. State a narrow contribution relative to actual prior work, a minimal experiment grid, feasible resource assumptions, and remaining user decisions. Provide proposed one-paragraph introduction wording and a four-week division of work in the task directory; preserve the existing proposal files until an integration assignment explicitly includes them.
acceptance: Recommendation traces to reviewed reports
No novelty or performance guarantee is made
Plan includes a feasibility milestone and actual unresolved choices
Draft is ready for user review without modifying unrelated existing work
